value.rationale: The minimal adjacent-corner detector pattern is canonical and qualitatively controllable, but its weakest decay mode is unexpectedly slow: for every fixed dimension its first-order loss rate scales as pi^(2d)/product(p_j^3), substantially smaller than the trap density product(2/p_j). Exact coefficient and unique extremal Fourier sector make a nontrivial, natural relaxation bottleneck and quantitative boundary for design of coherent sinks, not a restatement of known trap count.
